issues.description: Element: function simulate_msd_one_round. Template (template_repository/msd.py) constructs a Stim circuit with an argument: circ = stim.Circuit(n_shots). The reference solution (solution_repository/msd.py) constructs an empty Stim circuit with no arguments: circ = stim.Circuit(). This mismatch is about the constructor parameter(s) used for stim.Circuit and can mislead students into thinking they should pass the number of shots to the Circuit constructor. Passing n_shots to the constructor changes the meaning (it is a qubit-count style parameter in Stim, not a shots parameter) and will produce incorrect behavior or confusing runtime errors when students follow the template. The inconsistency between the template and solution therefore creates a structural confusion when implementing simulate_msd_one_round.
issues.suggestedFix: In the template, change the Stim circuit construction in simulate_msd_one_round from circ = stim.Circuit(n_shots) to circ = stim.Circuit(). Update any surrounding comments/docstring to indicate that shots are provided to the sampler (e.g., sim = circ.compile_sampler(); sim.sample(n_shots)) rather than to the Circuit constructor. Ensure any other examples in the template similarly avoid passing shot counts to stim.Circuit.
